}

No crash logs. Rotation while the dialog is open is the repro.
questions.promptHtml: Why two dialogs, and how do you fix it without introducing a new bug?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Dismiss the dialog in onDestroy." This misses that the FragmentManager restores DialogFragments itself; and there are two fragments, not a leaked window.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Is it a DialogFragment or a raw AlertDialog.show()? (DialogFragment, per code.) Does the repro need rotation, or does dark mode do it too? Did 8.4 change the pref write timing?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Add if (savedInstanceState == null) or a findFragmentByTag("notif") == null guard; one-line hotfix.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) The FragmentManager restored the dialog fragment from saved state during super.onCreate, then onCreate added a second one because the pref is still false, (b) tag collisions making show replace silently (no, show adds a new fragment under the same tag; both exist), (c) a double onCreate from another cause, (d) red herring: process death.
  4. How I'd verify each: adb shell dumpsys activity <pkg> and look at "Added Fragments:" showing two NotifPromptDialog entries; log supportFragmentManager.fragments.size in onCreate; reproduce with adb shell cmd uimode night yes.
  5. Root cause: Fragment state is saved with the Activity. On recreate, super.onCreate(savedInstanceState) re-adds the old DialogFragment and shows its dialog. The pref is only written on "Yes", so the condition is still true and the code shows another. Fragments aren't "re-shown by my code"; they're restored by the framework.
  6. Fix: Guard on restoration, and derive the visible state from a single source of truth.
override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
    super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
    setContentView(R.layout.home)
    val needsPrompt = !prefs.getBoolean("asked_notif", false)
    if (needsPrompt && supportFragmentManager.findFragmentByTag("notif") == null) {
        NotifPromptDialog().show(supportFragmentManager, "notif")
    }
}

Better: write asked_notif = true when the dialog is shown (or in the ViewModel as a one-shot event), and make "Not now" also persist, so the condition ends. 7. Prevention: Rule: anything shown from onCreate must be guarded by savedInstanceState == null or a findFragmentByTag. Instrumented test with recreate() while the dialog is up asserting fragments.size == 1. Lint/Detekt for .show( in onCreate. 8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I wouldn't use show() of a bare AlertDialog (it won't survive recreation and throws WindowLeaked). I wouldn't use commitAllowingStateLoss to paper over anything here. I'd keep it a DialogFragment so state restoration is free.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• What if the prompt result is delivered to the Activity via a listener set in onCreate? → Use the Fragment Result API (setFragmentResultListener) so it survives recreation (chunk 03).
  • Why does a raw AlertDialog produce "Activity has leaked window"? → It's attached to a destroyed Activity's window; dismiss it in onDestroy/onStop.
  • Would launchMode=singleTop fix it? → No, recreation isn't a new intent.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A composite of a ride-hailing app: a "rate your trip" dialog stacked 3-high for dark-mode users who switched at night. The fix was one-shot UI events modeled as state with an explicit consumed flag.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: Dismisses dialog in onDestroy or locks orientation.
  • Hire: Knows FragmentManager restores DialogFragment, adds a guard, fixes the pref write.
  • Strong hire: Uses dumpsys activity to prove, explains one-shot event modeling, adds a recreate test.

questions.subtopic: Locale, dark mode, font scale, density
questions.promptHtml: For locale, dark mode, font scale and display density changes, what actually happens inside the app, and how should each be handled?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Four triggers, each with different gotchas: shows whether you've handled accessibility and theming in production.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: All four are configuration changes, so the Activity is recreated and resources are resolved again: values-fr, values-night, sp text scaled by fontScale, and dp converted by density. My job is to make recreation safe and not hardcode pixels or cache resolved resources. For dark mode I use AppCompatDelegate or DayNight themes with values-night; for font scale I use sp for text only and test at 200%; for density I use dp and vector drawables; for locale I use resource folders and never concatenate strings.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
Change Config field What re-resolves Gotchas
Locale locales (LocaleList), layoutDirection values-xx, drawable-ldrtl, plurals Cached strings/formatters, RTL, number/date formats, Locale.getDefault() changed per process
Dark mode uiMode night bits values-night, drawable-night, theme DayNight Hardcoded colors, WebView force dark, images with white backgrounds
Font scale fontScale (and fontWeightAdjustment API 31) sp dimension values Clipped text in fixed-height containers; since Android 14 scaling goes up to 200% and is non-linear for large text (verify exact curve in docs)
Density densityDpi drawable-xxhdpi, dp -> px Bitmaps decoded at old density; Display size setting from the user

Mechanics: Resources objects are reconfigured by ResourcesManager; stale caches such as a Typeface, a Drawable kept in a singleton, or a precomputed px value are not updated.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
// Dark mode, app-level override (persist it yourself; AppCompat does not)
AppCompatDelegate.setDefaultNightMode(AppCompatDelegate.MODE_NIGHT_YES) // recreates Activities
// Density-safe conversions
val px = TypedValue.applyDimension(TypedValue.COMPLEX_UNIT_DIP, 16f, resources.displayMetrics)
<!-- values-night/colors.xml -->
<color name="surface">#121212</color>
<!-- text: sp; containers: wrap_content / minHeight, not fixed height -->
<TextView android:textSize="16sp" android:minHeight="48dp" />

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Fixed dp height for text containers, truncating at 200% font scale.
  • Using sp for icons and padding (they scale and break the layout).
  • Persisting resolved strings (translated text) in a DB or push token payload.
  • Forgetting that AppCompatDelegate.setDefaultNightMode doesn't persist across process restarts.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. How does MODE_NIGHT_FOLLOW_SYSTEM differ from system dark mode? → The first is the AppCompat default and follows uiMode; explicit modes override per-app.
  2. Why is Display size change a config change? → It changes densityDpi, screenWidthDp and others.
  3. How can you test font scale quickly? → adb shell settings put system font_scale 2.0.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Average: names each setting. Senior: ties each to its Configuration field, the dp/sp split, caching traps, accessibility testing at 200% and the persistence of overrides.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: An onboarding screen clipped the CTA at 175% font scale for ~3% of users (older users), cutting conversion; the fix was minHeight containers.

questions.promptHtml: How do per-app language preferences work on Android 13+, and how do you support them on older versions?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: A modern platform feature with a classic recreate side effect; checks if you know the LocaleManager / AppCompat split.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: On API 33+ the system exposes a per-app language picker in Settings, backed by LocaleManager. The app declares its supported languages in a localeConfig XML and can set it programmatically. Below 33, AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales() (AppCompat 1.6.0+) backports it, persisting the choice through a metadata-flagged service. Changing it triggers a locale configuration change, so Activities are recreated.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
• API 33: LocaleManager.getApplicationLocales() / setApplicationLocales(LocaleList); the OS stores it, applies it at app start, and restores it via backup.
  • android:localeConfig="@xml/locales_config" on <application> lists supported tags; Settings shows only those. AGP 8.1+ can generate it from res/resources.properties (unqualifiedResLocale=en-US) via androidResources { generateLocaleConfig = true }.
  • AppCompat: AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales(LocaleListCompat.forLanguageTags("fr")). On API 33+ it forwards to LocaleManager. Below 33 it needs AppCompatActivity (so the delegate can apply it), recreates the activities, and for persistence you add:
<service
    android:name="androidx.appcompat.app.AppLocalesMetadataHolderService"
    android:enabled="false"
    android:exported="false">
    <meta-data android:name="autoStoreLocales" android:value="true" />
</service>
  • Behaviour: it overrides the system locale only for your app; Application context may stay on the system locale until recreated, a source of mixed-language UI. Locale.getDefault() in your process reflects the app locale after it is applied.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales(LocaleListCompat.forLanguageTags("hi-IN"))
val current = AppCompatDelegate.getApplicationLocales() // empty = follow system
// Reset
AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales(LocaleListCompat.getEmptyLocaleList())

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Using ComponentActivity (not AppCompat) on API < 33 and finding the API has no effect.
  • Setting Configuration.setLocale() on the base context by hand and breaking WebView / resource caching.
  • Forgetting to add each language to localeConfig, so the Settings picker hides it.
  • Not calling it before content views are inflated at cold start on API < 33.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Does it survive reinstall/backup? → On 33+ the OS backs it up; on older versions your stored value goes with your own backup rules.
  2. What happens to server-side content language? → Send Accept-Language from the app locale, not the device default.
  3. What locale does the Application class see? → Possibly the system locale until the config is applied; avoid reading strings in Application.onCreate.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Average: "use setApplicationLocales". Senior: localeConfig, AGP generation, the pre-33 persistence service, recreation effect, and the stale-context traps.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Notification text was in English for users who picked Hindi in-app because a WorkManager worker built strings with the Application context before the locale was applied.

questions.contextHtml: After a release, a banking app (2.4M MAU, ~14% aged 55+) sees a 9% drop in "Pay" completion among users with large-font settings. Crashlytics shows no crash. QA verified only fontScale 1.3. Support screenshots show the "Pay" button clipped to half height, and some users who change font size while the app is open see the previous screen layout kept while the text is bigger. The Pay screen declares android:configChanges="fontScale|screenSize|orientation". The button is android:layout_height="48dp" with textSize="18sp"; one custom AmountView caches paint.textSize = 18 * resources.displayMetrics.scaledDensity in its constructor.
questions.promptHtml: Run the post-incident review: what happened, why was it missed, and how do you prevent a recurrence?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Remove the fixed height." That addresses one symptom and ignores the stale cache from configChanges, why QA missed it, and the process fix.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: What font scale distribution do affected users have (Settings range up to 130% or 200%)? Was the change a fixed-height refactor or configChanges? Which OS versions: Android 14+ supports up to 200%. Is the drop only on Pay or on other screens?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Hotfix: remove fontScale from configChanges so the screen recreates and re-reads resources; change the button to minHeight=48dp with wrap_content. Staged rollout 5%, verify.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) Fixed 48dp height cannot hold 18sp x 2.0 (plus padding), (b) configChanges="fontScale" stops recreation but the cached scaledDensity never refreshes, (c) unrelated: A/B test on Pay copy, (d) device-specific OEM font.
  4. How I'd verify each: adb shell settings put system font_scale 2.0; run through the flow; Layout Inspector; Paparazzi/Compose screenshot tests at 0.85/1.0/1.3/2.0; check Crashlytics custom keys for font scale; analytics cut by fontScale bucket.
  5. Root cause: Fixed container height assumed a text size that is a user-controlled variable (sp x scale). In addition, declaring fontScale in configChanges meant AmountView's constructor-time cached text size was stale. Also note DisplayMetrics.scaledDensity is deprecated (API 34 non-linear scaling makes a single multiplier incorrect; use TypedValue.applyDimension(COMPLEX_UNIT_SP, ...) or TypedValue.deriveDimension).
  6. Fix: Short term as in step 2. Long term: all text containers wrap_content / minHeight; remove scaledDensity use:
paint.textSize = TypedValue.applyDimension(
    TypedValue.COMPLEX_UNIT_SP, 18f, resources.displayMetrics)
// and recompute in View.onConfigurationChanged(newConfig) if the Activity handles fontScale
  1. Prevention: Screenshot tests across font scales in CI; a QA checklist item "200% font, bold text, display size large, dark mode"; lint rule for layout_height fixed dp on TextView/Button; accessibility scanner in CI.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I wouldn't cap font scaling in code (breaks accessibility and is a legal/compliance risk for banking). I would not keep configChanges for performance on a payment screen: correctness beats a faster rotation.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Bold text setting? → fontWeightAdjustment (API 31), also part of the config; heavier glyphs widen text.
  • Why not clamp at 1.3? → Accessibility guidelines (WCAG 1.4.4 resize to 200%); clamping excludes your core older users.
  • How do you cap one decorative label safely? → Use dp for that single label, with a design-system exception.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A composite of a healthcare app: clipped dosage text at 200% font was a patient-safety issue. We added a gated screenshot suite at 4 font scales and the issue class vanished.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: Only fixes the height, no process or other causes.
  • Hire: Finds both the fixed height and configChanges/cache issue; adds multi-scale testing.
  • Strong hire: Knows the API 34 non-linear scaling, scaledDensity deprecation, analytics by font bucket, and a staged rollout and CI guardrail.

questions.promptHtml: Describe the full state save and restore pipeline during a configuration change, and explain what makes recreation expensive.

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: A senior must reason about what runs on the main thread during a relaunch and why a slow onCreate turns rotation into jank.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: The system tears down the old instance (stop, save state, retain, destroy), then builds a new one: new Activity, window, inflation, fragments, view hierarchy restore, first measure/layout/draw. All of that is on the main thread, so cost is roughly inflation + fragment restore + binding + first frame. I reduce it by moving data into a ViewModel, keeping onCreate light, avoiding heavy init in views and using lazy or async work.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
The relaunch is driven by ATMS sending an ActivityRelaunchItem (a transaction) to the app. In the app process:

handleRelaunchActivity
  -> handleStopActivity (if resumed: onPause + onStop)
  -> onSaveInstanceState -> Bundle (state of window hierarchy, fragments, SavedStateRegistry)
  -> onRetainNonConfigurationInstance (ViewModelStore + custom object)
  -> performDestroyActivity (onDestroy)
  -> performLaunchActivity: new instance, attach, Application context, new Window/DecorView
  -> onCreate(Bundle) -> setContentView (inflate) -> fragments restored (FragmentManager.restoreSaveState)
  -> onStart -> onRestoreInstanceState (restoreHierarchyState) -> onResume
  -> ViewRootImpl: first traversal (measure, layout, draw) + new surface

Cost drivers: XML inflation of deep hierarchies (reflection-free but still tens of ms on low-end CPUs), RecyclerView rebuilding and rebinding, image decoding (Bitmaps recycled with the old window), Fragment re-creation and view binding, and any work in onCreate/onStart that isn't skipped by savedInstanceState != null. Binder calls (WindowManager, ActivityTaskManager, config service) add fixed overhead (~ms) per relaunch.

Rough budget on a mid-range device: teardown 20-40 ms, inflate 50-150 ms for a complex screen, first frame 30-80 ms. Over 200 ms users see a flash. Measure it, don't guess.

Reduction techniques: keep expensive data in a ViewModel so rebinding is just submitList with an already loaded list; use ViewStub/lazy inflation for rare content; retain image caches in an app-scoped cache (Coil/Glide memory caches are app-wide); avoid re-fetching in onStart; configChanges for a handful of heavy, self-contained screens (player, map, game) only when it is correct.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
Trace it:

override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
    Trace.beginSection("Home.onCreate")
    super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
    setContentView(R.layout.home)
    Trace.endSection()
}
// adb: python systrace / Perfetto with "view" and "am" categories, look at "activityRestart"

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Doing disk or network in onCreate, multiplying the cost by every recreation.
  • Treating savedInstanceState as data store for lists (Bundle limit ~1 MB shared per transaction; see process death chunk).
  • Recreating heavyweight objects (OkHttpClient, Gson) in Activity fields.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Where does onSaveInstanceState get its view state from? → Window.saveHierarchyState() stores SparseArray<Parcelable> keyed by view id under android:viewHierarchyState.
  2. Does the Activity's Window survive? → No, a new PhoneWindow, DecorView and ViewRootImpl are created; a new surface is allocated.
  3. Why does the launch feel slower than a cold fragment replace? → The whole window/viewroot is rebuilt, not just a subtree.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Average: "it destroys and recreates and calls onCreate again". Senior: names the stages, quantifies cost, identifies main-thread drivers and a measurement tool, and gives reduction techniques.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A feed screen took ~420 ms to relaunch on 3 GB devices because onCreate parsed a JSON config from disk each time; moving it to the app scope cut it to ~110 ms.

questions.promptHtml: Mechanically, how does a ViewModelStore get from the destroyed Activity to the new one, and in which cases does it get cleared or lost?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Separates people who memorised "ViewModel survives rotation" from people who know the platform retains the store, and can reason about edge cases such as process death and multiple instances.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: ComponentActivity implements onRetainNonConfigurationInstance() and returns a holder containing its ViewModelStore. ActivityThread keeps that object on the ActivityClientRecord while the old Activity is destroyed and passes it to the new instance, which retrieves it with getLastNonConfigurationInstance() in ComponentActivity.ensureViewModelStore(). A lifecycle observer clears the store on ON_DESTROY unless isChangingConfigurations() is true. It is lost on process death.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
Activity#1.onRetainNonConfigurationInstance()
   -> NonConfigurationInstances { custom, viewModelStore }
ActivityThread: r.lastNonConfigurationInstances = ... (kept in ActivityClientRecord)
Activity#2.attach(..., lastNonConfigurationInstances)
Activity#2.getViewModelStore():
   ensureViewModelStore(): getLastNonConfigurationInstance()?.viewModelStore ?: ViewModelStore()
  • isChangingConfigurations() is set in performDestroyActivity for a relaunch, so the observer skips clear().
  • Fragments: FragmentManagerViewModel is itself a ViewModel in the host's store, holding the child ViewModelStores per fragment; a Fragment's own ViewModels are cleared when its FragmentManager decides it's removed for good (popped from back stack, remove and no config change).
  • Edge cases: when the Activity is stopped in the background and the system kills the process, there is no retained object; with Don't keep activities the Activity is finished/destroyed without being a config change, so the store is cleared (that's why ViewModels reset in that mode: it simulates "destroyed", not "config changed").
  • Multiple instances: each Activity instance has its own store; two instances of the same class in the back stack have separate ViewModels.
  • Historical note: onRetainCustomNonConfigurationInstance is deprecated; use ViewModel.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
// Simplified view of the observer inside ComponentActivity
lifecycle.addObserver(LifecycleEventObserver { _, event ->
    if (event == Lifecycle.Event.ON_DESTROY) {
        if (!isChangingConfigurations) viewModelStore.clear()
    }
})

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Thinking "Don't keep activities" proves ViewModel survival; it clears it.
  • Holding the Activity in the ViewModel: the retained object then pins the destroyed Activity until the ViewModel clears.
  • Assuming by viewModels() in a Fragment returns the Activity's instance (it is scoped to the Fragment).

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. What if the user presses Home and the system kills the process? → Everything in memory is gone; SavedStateHandle data comes back through the Bundle on next launch.
  2. Does activityViewModels() survive Fragment replacement? → Yes, it is tied to the Activity's store.
  3. How does Navigation's hiltNavGraphViewModels get scoped? → A NavBackStackEntry owns its own store; it clears when the entry is popped.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Average: "ViewModel survives configuration changes via a ViewModelStore". Senior: names the hook, ActivityThread retention, the isChangingConfigurations guard, and the effects on fragments and developer options.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A QA engineer used "Don't keep activities" to test rotation state and filed false bugs because ViewModels were cleared; the team updated the test guide to use real rotation and ActivityScenario.recreate().

questions.promptHtml: How do foldables, split-screen and freeform windows change how you think about configuration changes?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Large-screen behaviour is a top-tier skill gap; orientation is no longer the right abstraction.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: Resizing is now continuous and independent of rotation: a window can be resized by dragging, unfolding or entering split-screen, which delivers screenSize/smallestScreenSize/screenLayout config changes. By default that recreates the Activity every time, so state handling must be airtight. I build layouts from window size classes using Jetpack WindowManager, not orientation, avoid assuming display size equals window size, and I treat posture (tabletop/book) as separate information from WindowInfoTracker.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
• Since Android 7.0, apps targeting API 24+ are resizable by default (android:resizeableActivity defaults to true). Android 12L/13 improved large-screen behaviour (taskbar, letterboxing rules for non-resizable apps, activity embedding).
  • Window size ≠ display size. Use WindowMetricsCalculator.getOrCreate().computeCurrentWindowMetrics(activity) (Jetpack WindowManager) or WindowMetrics (API 30+), not Display.getRealSize.
  • Size classes: Compact < 600dp, Medium 600-839dp, Expanded >= 840dp width (and height classes 480/900dp).
  • WindowInfoTracker.getOrCreate(context).windowLayoutInfo(activity) emits FoldingFeature (state: FLAT/HALF_OPENED, orientation, occlusion type).
  • Config changes while folding: screenSize|smallestScreenSize|screenLayout change. Activities that declare these in configChanges get onConfigurationChanged and must resize themselves; many foldable-first apps do so, but it requires verifying that nothing depends on layout-w.
  • Android 16 (API 36): for apps targeting 36, on displays >= 600dp, manifest/runtime orientation, aspect ratio and resizability restrictions are ignored, so the Activity must be fully adaptive; temporary opt-out is available for apps targeting 36 and removed for 37 (verify on developer.android.com, behavior changes for Android 16).
  • Multi-resume (Android 10+): in multi-window, multiple Activities can be RESUMED at once (onTopResumedActivityChanged tells which has focus); camera/mic etc. should be held by the focused one.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
lifecycleScope.launch {
    repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) {
        WindowInfoTracker.getOrCreate(this@MainActivity)
            .windowLayoutInfo(this@MainActivity)
            .collect { info ->
                val fold = info.displayFeatures.filterIsInstance<FoldingFeature>().firstOrNull()
                vm.onPosture(fold?.state, fold?.orientation)
            }
    }
}
val widthDp = WindowMetricsCalculator.getOrCreate()
    .computeCurrentWindowMetrics(this).bounds.width() / resources.displayMetrics.density

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Using resources.configuration.orientation as a proxy for "tablet layout".
  • Locking orientation or assuming Display.getSize equals app window size.
  • Releasing camera in onPause, which fires in multi-window when another window is focused (but you are still visible).
  • Hard-coding insets for a gesture bar when on a freeform window.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. What does resizeableActivity="false" do today? → Large screens put the app in compat/letterbox mode; behaviour changes with API 36 targeting on large displays (verify).
  2. Folded to unfolded: what config bits move? → smallestScreenWidthDp, screenWidthDp/HeightDp, screenLayout, and sometimes density if display changes.
  3. How do you preserve a video across unfold? → Keep the player in a ViewModel/service or handle the config yourself and just resize the surface.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Average: "use sw600dp layouts and avoid portrait lock". Senior: continuous resize model, WindowManager APIs, posture, multi-resume focus rules and version-specific policy.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A scanner app released camera in onPause, so in split-screen the preview went black whenever the user tapped the other app; moving release to onStop fixed it.

questions.contextHtml: A marketplace app (10M MAU, 40% on devices with 3 GB RAM or less, median device Snapdragon 4-series) shows p95 rotation time of 900 ms from Firebase Performance custom trace ("config_change_ttfd") and 2% of rotations produce ANR-adjacent frame drops (Choreographer: "Skipped 54 frames!"). The product screen has a 6-level nested LinearLayout, a ViewPager2 with 3 fragments, a RecyclerView of 40 items, and Retrofit calls fired in onStart. Traces show: inflate 310 ms, fragment restore 140 ms, onStart network call dispatch and JSON parse on main for cached response 90 ms, bitmap decode 180 ms. Red herring: Hilt component creation takes 6 ms.
questions.promptHtml: Bring p95 under 300 ms. What do you change, in what order, and what would you refuse to do?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Add configChanges for rotation." That trades correctness for a metric, ignores dark mode and font-scale recreations, and doesn't address the main-thread work that also hurts cold start.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Is the 900 ms measured from onPause to first frame, or only onCreate? What's the split by device RAM and OS? Which config changes dominate (rotation or uiMode)? Are fragments stateful or reloading from the network? Is the product images flow cached?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Move JSON parse and cache read off main and out of onStart; drive from the ViewModel so recreation does not redo it. This alone saves ~90 ms with a low-risk change.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) Inflation of nested layouts (310 ms), (b) bitmap re-decoding because the image pipeline isn't hitting memory cache (180 ms), (c) fragment restore reconstructing three pages eagerly (140 ms), (d) network/JSON in onStart (90 ms), (e) DI cost: no (6 ms).
  4. How I'd verify each: Perfetto trace on a real low-end device with view, gfx, am, res categories; Android Studio Layout Inspector for depth; Glide/Coil logs for cache hit rate; Macrobenchmark with FrameTimingMetric and a rotation scenario; method tracing for onStart.
  5. Root cause: Everything is recomputed on the main thread because the ViewModel doesn't own the loaded model, the image cache isn't keyed to survive, and the layout is deep.
  6. Fix: Flatten the hierarchy with ConstraintLayout (310 ms -> ~120 ms), set offscreenPageLimit default and make secondary page fragments lazy (FragmentStateAdapter), ensure Coil/Glide memory cache has the target size key and doesn't downsample differently per orientation (decode once for Size.ORIGINAL/same bounds), move data loading into the ViewModel with stateIn(WhileSubscribed(5000)) so rotation keeps the collector alive for 5 s, and use RecyclerView.setHasFixedSize(true) + DiffUtil with ListAdapter plus a RecycledViewPool cached in the ViewModel isn't recommended (leaks contexts). Target: 120 + 70 + 40 + 0 = ~230 ms plus teardown.
  7. Prevention: Macrobenchmark rotation scenario in CI with a budget (e.g. p95 <= 300 ms on a reference low-end device); trace instrumentation in onCreate; code review rule for "no IO in lifecycle callbacks".
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I'd not use configChanges globally. I'd consider it only for the fullscreen gallery. I wouldn't cache a View hierarchy across recreations (leaks the Activity).

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Memory spike during rotation causes OOM? → Old and new windows briefly coexist; bitmaps double. Use hardware bitmaps or shared bitmap pool, and largeHeap is a last resort.
  • Can't change the layout this quarter? → Do the data and image work first (~270 ms of the 720 ms).
  • How to make the metric trustworthy? → Measure with Perfetto-based reportFullyDrawn and the same device across builds.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A composite: the biggest win in a catalog app wasn't layout work but a bitmap cache key that included orientation, so every rotation was a 100% cache miss. One key change dropped p95 rotation by 40%.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: configChanges or portrait lock.
  • Hire: Moves work off main, uses ViewModel, reduces inflation, measures.
  • Strong hire: Explains cache-key bug, lazy pages, benchmark budget in CI, memory doubling during relaunch, and refuses the global configChanges shortcut with reasons.

questions.contextHtml:
A news app (3M DAU) gets increasing OutOfMemoryError after 15-20 rotations in a session; heap grows ~18 MB per rotation (Android Studio heap dump: 22 instances of ArticleActivity, retained size 14 MB each). Crash rate for OOM is 0.4% of sessions, concentrated on 2 GB devices. Code excerpt:

class ArticleViewModel : ViewModel() {
    var listener: ((Article) -> Unit)? = null     // set by Activity
    lateinit var headerView: ImageView             // cached "to avoid re-finding"
    private val _article = MutableLiveData<Article>()
    val article: LiveData<Article> = _article
    fun load(id: String) = viewModelScope.launch {
        _article.value = repo.get(id)
        listener?.invoke(_article.value!!)
    }
}
class ArticleActivity : AppCompatActivity() {
    private val vm: ArticleViewModel by viewModels()
    override fun onCreate(b: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(b)
        setContentView(R.layout.article)
        vm.headerView = findViewById(R.id.header)
        vm.listener = { a -> title = a.title }     // captures this
        vm.load(intent.getStringExtra("id")!!)
    }
}

LeakCanary reports: GC ROOT thread ... → ArticleViewModel.listener → ArticleActivity$onCreate$1 → ArticleActivity (destroyed).
questions.promptHtml: Explain why heaps grow only on rotation, why it's 22 instances and not 1, and how you fix and prevent it.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Set the listener to null in onDestroy." That patches one leak but leaves headerView, and does not teach the structural rule.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Does the leak reproduce on back press (no: ViewModel is cleared then), or only rotation? Any other static/singleton holders? Is it the same on dark mode?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Hotfix: null listener and headerView in onDestroy guarded by isChangingConfigurations, ship with staged rollout. It stops growth immediately.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) ViewModel fields hold the Activity/View, (b) Hilt/Singleton retains the Activity, (c) a leaked Handler or coroutine in lifecycleScope, (d) bitmap cache growth (red herring: instances count points to Activity).
  4. How I'd verify each: LeakCanary (reference chain shown above), Android Studio heap dump filtered by ArticleActivity instance count, adb shell dumpsys meminfo <pkg> for Activities: count, repeat rotation test 20x.
  5. Root cause: ViewModel outlives the Activity instance across config changes. Each rotation, the new Activity writes itself into vm.listener and vm.headerView, but the previous instance is held until overwritten; the real growth happens because the headerView ImageView retains its Context (the destroyed Activity), and each Activity also has a window decor and bitmaps. Instance count 22 happens when the overwritten references are not the only holders: viewModelScope.launch coroutine captured listener mid-load, and in-flight loads during repeated rotation keep older lambdas alive.
  6. Fix: Strictly one-way flow: ViewModel exposes state, Activity observes.
class ArticleViewModel(private val repo: Repo) : ViewModel() {
    private val _ui = MutableStateFlow<Article?>(null)
    val ui = _ui.asStateFlow()
    fun load(id: String) { viewModelScope.launch { _ui.value = repo.get(id) } }
}
// Activity
lifecycleScope.launch {
    repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) { vm.ui.filterNotNull().collect { title = it.title } }
}
  1. Prevention: LeakCanary in debug builds with rotation instrumentation test (recreate() 10x, assert Activity count); lint/detekt rule forbidding View/Context/Activity types in ViewModel classes (StaticFieldLeak); review checklist.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I wouldn't use WeakReference for the listener as a primary fix (hides the design problem, lifetime gets unpredictable). I wouldn't use largeHeap to hide it.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Would SharedFlow events cause the same? → Only if collected beyond lifecycle; use repeatOnLifecycle.
  • Does AndroidViewModel(application) solve it? → For Context, yes (Application context), not for Views or lambdas capturing Activity.
  • Why only rotation, not back press? → onCleared drops the whole ViewModel on finish.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A composite: a "temporary" lateinit var view in a ViewModel for a screenshot feature produced 0.3% OOMs for months; it was only found after a recreate-N-times test was added.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: Only nulls the listener.
  • Hire: Identifies ViewModel-outlives-Activity, removes view/lambda references, one-way state.
  • Strong hire: Adds automated recreate-loop test, lint rule, explains instance counting, and rejects WeakReference/largeHeap with reasons.

questions.contextHtml: A new engineering manager at a 40-engineer fintech Android team wants to reduce "state loss" bugs (11 open tickets this quarter, all reproduced on rotation or dark mode). She proposes a policy: add android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize|screenLayout|smallestScreenSize|keyboardHidden|uiMode|locale|layoutDirection|fontScale|density" to every Activity and lock portrait on phones. The app has 1 Activity per feature (14), a few fragments with retained state, and a ViewModel layer used inconsistently. Target SDK 34, 25% of users on tablets and foldables, 6% use accessibility font scale >= 1.5.
questions.promptHtml: What do you recommend? Include what you'd tell her and the team, and how you'd measure success.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "That's a bad idea, it's discouraged." No quantified alternatives, no consideration of her goal (fewer state-loss tickets), no migration plan.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Are the 11 bugs unique root causes or 3 patterns? What fraction of sessions have a recreation (instrument it)? How many screens already use ViewModel+SavedStateHandle? Is process death part of the ticket set? What are the tablet/foldable usage numbers and revenue share?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Triage the 11 bugs; fix the patterns (unguarded onCreate work, state held in Activity fields, dialogs). For the 2-3 worst screens, apply a targeted fix, not a global switch.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) State kept in Activities/Fragments instead of ViewModel (most likely), (b) one-shot events re-fired on recreation, (c) missing ids/state in custom views, (d) retained fragments with stale references.
  4. How I'd verify each: Reproduce all 11 with adb shell cmd uimode night yes, font_scale, and ActivityScenario.recreate(), then cluster by root cause. Add telemetry: count of isChangingConfigurations destroys per session.
  5. Root cause: The state ownership model is inconsistent, not the platform's recreation. configChanges would only hide one trigger in the tests she runs, while production keeps process death, multi-window and any bit not declared (fontWeightAdjustment, colorMode, grammaticalGender, plus the whole class on API 34+ new bits). It would also make layout-w/values-night stop applying automatically, creating new stale UI bugs, and portrait lock gets ignored on large screens in newer targets.
  6. Fix: Policy: "state lives in ViewModel+SavedStateHandle or persistence; Activities may be destroyed at any time". Provide a template (base ViewModel, UiState, one-shot event helper), a recreate test harness, and a lint/detekt rule. configChanges allowed by exception (player/map/game) with a checklist.
  7. Prevention: CI instrumented test that recreates each feature Activity and asserts visible state; add "Don't keep activities" and font-scale to QA. Dashboard for state-loss tickets.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: I'd not adopt the global switch: it is a cheap win in the first sprint and an expensive bug class later. I'd also not tell her "never": pure fullscreen media screens can handle config themselves.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• She insists for a deadline? → Offer a time-boxed experiment on 3 screens plus a recreation test suite; compare ticket rates in 4 weeks.
  • What about Compose screens? → State via rememberSaveable + ViewModel; recomposition handles config naturally (A3).
  • Is there any scenario where global configChanges is right? → A kiosk/embedded device app with fixed hardware and no user locale or font changes.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A composite: a team shipped global configChanges for a quarter; tickets fell, then spiked after Android 12L tablets arrived because layouts didn't update on split-screen. The migration back cost two sprints.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: Agrees or rejects without analysis.
  • Hire: Explains why it hides bugs, offers state ownership fix, proposes tests.
  • Strong hire: Quantifies, measures recreation frequency, uses exceptions policy, ties to large-screen/accessibility share, and gives a rollout and success metric.
